theOneSharedCauseTheGrantAskedAbout.question: Are the two COMPONENT_SET failures the same defect?
theOneSharedCauseTheGrantAskedAbout.answer: ONE CAUSE, and it is neither of the two causes the committed records name. Both families are Colorado sealing routes whose own Judicial Department guide names a FOUR-document set, and both deliver the motion and the granting order and omit the notice and the second order. The four omitted documents -- JDF 614 and JDF 613 for the conviction route, JDF 493 and JDF 492 for the non-conviction route -- are all recorded in the committed corpus index in EXACTLY ONE custody, nationwide_recovery_pool_2026_09_02, and in no other. That single custody is the whole of the overlap, and it is the cause.
theOneSharedCauseTheGrantAskedAbout.whatShowedIt: Reading data/rcap-all50/local-source-corpus-index.json rather than either family's own record. VF22 concluded that JDF 492 and JDF 493 'appear NOWHERE ... not anywhere under STATES/CO in the master library, so they are a source-acquisition gap as well as a component gap'. That is true of the Master Library and false of the index as a whole: the index carries LegalEase Colorado/JDF492.pdf and LegalEase Colorado/reference-only/JDF-493__order-and-notice-of-hearing-to-seal-non-conviction-records__rev-2019-08.pdf, in the same recovery-pool custody where the conviction family's manifest had already placed JDF 613 and JDF 614. The two families are also structurally identical form for form: JDF 612/613/614/615 maps onto JDF 477/492/493/478 as motion, denial order, order-and-notice-of-hearing, granting order, all at revision 2024-08-07 except JDF 493.
theOneSharedCauseTheGrantAskedAbout.andTheRecordedREASONWasWrongInBOTH: The conviction manifest said the binaries 'sit in custody nationwide_recovery_pool_2026_09_02, which no packet-factory container mounts, so neither can be bound by SHA-256 and neither may be rendered.' This lane measured that and it is false here. The index's own custodies array DECLARES that custody at root private/source-imports/Nationwide_Recovery_Pool_2026-09-02 with pathsRelativeTo custodyRoot; it is mounted in this worktree; and all four binaries hash on disk to exactly the digests the committed index records (measured, not quoted -- see sourceDigestsHashedByThisLane). data/rcap-grade-a/packet-factory-24h/PRIVATE_CUSTODY_MOUNT.json already recorded that a lane can see this custody absent because private/ is gitignored, and that its absence from a checkout proves nothing about custody.
theOneSharedCauseTheGrantAskedAbout.whatActuallyBlocksTheRender: The committed index does not IDENTIFY those entries. Every one of the four recovery-pool rows carries formNumber null and assetClass null. Both builders' resolveSources() selects an official form by state + formNumber + assetClass "FORM" and only then hashes it, so no build can bind a binary the index does not identify, and binding by file name would rest the packet's source claim on a file name. This is true in every container, mounted or not, which is why both builders now state it from the committed index and assert it there, rather than from what happens to be on disk.
theOneSharedCauseTheGrantAskedAbout.oneExceptionInsideTheOneCause: JDF 493 is additionally blocked by its own bytes and would still not render if the index identified it. The held copy is revision 2019-08 against a guide revised 2024-08-07; the index records acroFormPresent false, acroFieldCount 0, structuralClassObserved flat_pdf; and the guide tells a filer to complete '§§ A-C' on a document that has no lettered sections at all. So three of the four are owed a source-identity determination and the fourth is owed acquisition at the named revision. That distinction is now recorded per component instead of all four reading as 'missing'.

defectOneWrongField.howItWasFixed: The fact now holds the street alone, which is what scripts/rcap-official-forms/rcap-field-semantics.mjs declares participant.street_address to be -- its descriptor's refuseWhen rejects a caption naming a city, a state or a ZIP -- and what this family's municipal sibling has always held. Recorded as an advisory finding in build-findings.json. Closing it means changing scripts/rcap-official-forms/**, which every family shares.

whatThisLaneCouldNotRepair.why: Four official binaries are held at their indexed digests in a mounted custody the committed corpus index does not identify: every one of the four rows carries formNumber null and assetClass null. Classifying a corpus entry is a source-identity determination with its own governance -- scripts/grade-a-packet-factory-24h/generate-source-identity-findings.mjs, generate-source-relationship-registry.mjs, repin-lapsed-source-identities.mjs -- and a packet-repair lane that wrote an identity into the index would be certifying a source in order to let its own family pass. The corpus index is also generated, not hand-maintained.
whatThisLaneCouldNotRepair.whoIsOwedWhat: A source-identity determination over the nationwide_recovery_pool_2026_09_02 Colorado entries would unblock JDF 613, JDF 614 and JDF 492. It would NOT unblock JDF 493, which needs acquisition at the revision JDF 491 R: August 7, 2024 names. Note also that the custody declares itself PARTIAL_NATIONWIDE_RECOVERY_POOL and 'satisfies an individual source obligation and never a completeness assertion', so binding from it and asserting set completeness are separate questions for whoever owns them.
whatThisLaneCouldNotRepair.andBuildingThoseComponentsIsSeparateWork: Even once identified, each of JDF 613, JDF 614 and JDF 492 needs a field-map dictionary of its own -- 13, 16 and 13 widgets, all with the caption band Group_CourtType / County / Court Address / ∆ / Case Number / Division / Courtroom that these builders already handle -- and both builders assert their widget set against the dictionary in both directions, so none of it can be half-done. This lane did not start it, because a component the manifest declares undelivered and the index cannot bind must not be rendered from a file name.
